name: Bugis
notes: Buginese (Basa Ugi) — South Sulawesi (Austronesian) language of Indonesia, ~5 million speakers. Traditionally written in the Lontara script, a Brahmic-descended abugida (each of the 23 base consonant letters carries an inherent /a/, modified by post-base vowel diacritics; `inherent_vowel: 'a'` declares this generically per AGENTS.md rule 1/3, not as language-specific code), and today also in the Latin script; this spec covers LONTARA. GRAPHEME KEYS: the 23-letter base inventory (Sirk 1983; 'Lontara script' Wikipedia) maps one letter to one onset consonant (`ᨕ` is the glottal-onset/vowel-carrier letter, per the phoneme inventory's /ʔ/) plus five vowel diacritics. THREE letters (`ᨃ` ngka, `ᨇ` mpa, `ᨏ` nca) are PRENASALIZED-CONSONANT letters and earn their multigraph value under design-constraint test 2 -- exactly the Bantu ⟨mb⟩ /mb/ case named in AGENTS.md: the Lontara script devotes one letter to the whole nasal+obstruent onset, so /ŋk mp ntʃ/ are single orthographic units, not a k/p/tʃ letter preceded by a nasal letter. `ᨋ` (nra) is likewise kept as one unit (/nr/) rather than decomposed. KNOWN GAP, documented per AGENTS.md rule 4 rather than resolved by enumeration: Lontara is a DEFECTIVE script -- coda (final) consonants and consonant gemination are systematically NOT written at all (Sirk 1983), so this grapheme table cannot and does not recover them; a word ending in a coda consonant will transcribe as open, a genuine, cited limitation of the writing system itself, not a spec gap to fill. STRESS: Sirk (1983) describes Buginese stress as regular penultimate and non-contrastive; left unencoded, a documented exemption. TIER: no WikiPron (or other registrable) gold exists for `bug` (checked against CUNY-CL/wikipron's scrape summary, 2026-08-03: zero rows), so `skeleton`, not `research`.
